newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT--Dollar outlook brightest versus yen.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT--Dollar outlook brightest versus yen.

text.p: While the dollar's outlook is mixed against major currencies, its brightest near-term prospects are versus the Japanese yen, technical analysts said on Monday.

However, the gains the dollar may score versus the yen could undermine its strength against the mark -- the likely beneficiary of a weakening yen and uncertainty about the Europe Monetary Union, they added.
In afternoon trading, the dollar was quoted at 1.6905/08 marks versus 1.6945/55 at the close on Friday, and also at 123.69/74 yen vs 123.45/55.
Senior technical analyst Scott Siller at MCM CurrencyWatch is among the chartists who see further upside on dollar/yen, including a possible retest of the recent high of 124.82, set on February 14.
Siller noted dollar/yen bounced off session lows in the 123.00/25 area on both Friday and Monday, which pointed "to a continuation higher, with possibly a retest of 124.82."
The MCM CurrencyWatch analyst expected dollar/yen to retain an upward momentum unless it breaches 123.20 support.
"Dollar/yen should stay firm, along with mark/yen, and dollar/mark would struggle because of that," Siller added.
In a confirmation of the Japanese currency's all-around weakness, mark/yen started the week by taking out resistance at 72.90.

"The next upside goal is in the 73.40/80 zone," Siller further said. "We're looking at a well-defined bull channel to 73.30/40, although, looking at the hourly charts, mark/yen is slightly overbought."
Mark/yen was quoted at 73.15/18 in late Monday trading.
Past 73.30, mark/yen should target resistance at 73.80 and 74.50 -- a level that comes in a long-term trendline going back to August 1990, just off a high of 95.80.
Siller and other chartists were less bullish on dollar/mark.

"If dollar/mark loses 1.6850, this could take us to 1.6675 marks," said the MCM CurrencyWatch analyst who did not rule out "a near-term correction in mark/yen which would be bullish for dollar/mark over the near term, and take us possibly up to 1.70 marks again."
Dollar/Swiss continued to lag dollar/mark but is unlikely to send truly bearish signals for the dollar unless the 1.45 level goes, chartits said.
